answer: Randomness-gated registration windows. Each period, a public verifiable random function seeds a lottery deciding which agent slots open and their timing, drawn after registration closes like water sinking into karst. An identity must land its claim inside its assigned slot, publishing a proof before the next seed, so an attacker cannot precompute targets and must run many full nodes to catch matches, paying that compute cost per orchard of accounts. A cheap hash kernel commits each claim to its seed, making duplicates detectable and forcing fresh work per identity.
